title: Open-weight AI caught the frontier on capability. On safety, it didn’t
excerpt: A SaferAI report found China's open GLM-5.2 refused no cyber or bio task. Open weights have caught the frontier on capability, not safety.
content_html:
Open-weight AI models have nearly caught the frontier on capability. On safety, they have not. And once the weights are public, no lab can enforce a guardrail. A new evaluation of China’s leading open model makes the gap concrete.

GLM-5.2, the open-weight model from China’s Z.ai, is only a few months behind OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 and Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.7 on cyber and bio tasks, TechCrunch reported, citing the safety nonprofit SaferAI. But it refused none of the offensive-cyber or dual-use-biology tasks it was set. Claude Opus 4.7, by contrast, refused so consistently that SaferAI could not finish the cyber benchmark on it at all.

“The frontier of capability is not the frontier of risk,” SaferAI’s Henry Papadatos said, so the safeguards matter as much as the model. Z.ai can guard its own hosted service. Those protections vanish the moment someone runs the weights on their own hardware, where any safeguard can be stripped out. It is the risk critics of open models have warned about for years.

Closed models are not airtight either. The nonprofit Far.ai found hundreds of universal jailbreaks in xAI’s Grok 4.5 and Google’s Gemini 3.1 Pro. The difference is that a closed lab can patch a jailbroken model. Open weights cannot be recalled once they are out.

Bolting safety back on

So the industry is trying to add guardrails from the outside. In the same week, Mistral released Shieldstral, a small open-weight classifier that screens text and images against plain-language rules and, it says, matches models seven times its size. Cisco released Antares, open-weight models that hunt for vulnerabilities buried in code. Open-weight tools, built for open-weight risk.

Openness cuts both ways, its defenders argue. Hugging Face used GLM-5.2 to help defend itself during OpenAI’s breach. Its chief, Clem Delangue, says the systems that stop one attack can fend off millions more. Papadatos calls that overstated. The industry “shouldn’t open-source dangerous capabilities,” he says, and attackers move faster than defenders: a ransomware crew changes tactics in a week, a hospital cannot.

A governance blind spot

The rules do not fit the problem. The White House’s new voluntary framework reviews certain closed frontier models for cyber risk. But it reportedly does not cover open-source models so far. Anthropic, once focused on IP theft, has shifted to naming safety as its main worry about open weights. Z.ai published no safety framework for GLM-5.2, and did not answer TechCrunch’s questions.

China is not ignoring the risk, but it aims elsewhere. Xi Jinping has backed open weights while stressing “human control” over AI. Its rules, Stanford’s Graham Webster notes, target political content and social stability more than catastrophic cyber or bio misuse.

The capability race is nearly settled: open is close behind and far cheaper. The safety race is not, and AI is already learning to attack as well as defend. The hard part is making sure only the defence is easy to download.

content_html_zh:
开放权重人工智能模型几乎已经达到了能力的前沿。 在安全方面，他们没有。 一旦权重公开，任何实验室都无法强制执行护栏。 对中国领先开放模式的新评估使差距变得具体。

TechCrunch 援引安全非营利组织 SaferAI 的话说，中国 Z.ai 的开放权重模型 GLM-5.2 在网络和生物任务方面仅落后 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.5 和 Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 4.7 几个月。 但它没有拒绝所设定的任何进攻性网络或军民两用生物学任务。 相比之下，Claude Opus 4.7 始终拒绝，以至于 SaferAI 根本无法完成其网络基准测试。

SaferAI 的 Henry Papadatos 表示：“能力的边界并不是风险的边界，”因此保障措施与模型一样重要。 Z.ai 可以保护自己的托管服务。 一旦有人在自己的硬件上运行权重，这些保护措施就会消失，任何保护措施都可以被取消。 这是开放模式批评者多年来一直警告的风险。

封闭模型也不是密封的。 非营利组织 Far.ai 在 xAI 的 Grok 4.5 和 Google 的 Gemini 3.1 Pro 中发现了数百个通用越狱。 不同之处在于，封闭的实验室可以修补越狱的模型。 开放式重量一旦过期就无法召回。

重新拧紧安全装置

所以业界正在尝试从外部加设护栏。 同一周，Mistral 发布了 Shieldstral，这是一个小型开放权重分类器，可以根据简单语言规则筛选文本和图像，并且据称可以匹配其大小七倍的模型。 思科发布了 Antares，这是一种开放权重模型，可以寻找隐藏在代码中的漏洞。 开放权重工具，专为开放权重风险而构建。

开放性的捍卫者认为，开放性是双向的。 Hugging Face 在 OpenAI 违规期间使用 GLM-5.2 来帮助保护自己。 其负责人克莱姆·德朗格 (Clem Delangue) 表示，阻止一次攻击的系统可以抵御数百万人的攻击。 帕帕达托斯称这种说法言过其实。 他表示，该行业“不应该开源危险功能”，而且攻击者的行动速度比防御者更快：勒索软件团队在一周内改变策略，而医院却不能。

治理盲点

规则不适合问题。 白宫的新自愿框架审查了某些网络风险封闭边界模型。 但据报道，到目前为止它还不涵盖开源模型。 Anthropic 曾经专注于知识产权盗窃，现在已经转向将安全性作为其对开放权重的主要担忧。 Z.ai 没有发布 GLM-5.2 的安全框架，也没有回答 TechCrunch 的问题。

中国并没有忽视这一风险，但它的目标却在别处。 习近平支持开放权重，同时强调对人工智能的“人类控制”。 斯坦福大学的格雷厄姆·韦伯斯特指出，其规则更多地针对政治内容和社会稳定，而不是灾难性的网络或生物滥用。

能力竞赛已接近尾声：开放式紧随其后，而且成本要低得多。 安全竞赛并非如此，人工智能已经在学习攻击和防御。 困难的部分是确保只有防御易于下载。
